installation.note: nl is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The nl command numbers lines in files, similar to 'cat -n' but with more formatting options. It can number all lines, only non-empty lines, or lines matching specific patterns. Useful for adding line numbers to code, logs, or any text file.
when_to_use: Add line numbers to text files
Reference specific lines in code or logs

syntax.description: If no file is specified, nl reads from standard input. Line numbers are added to the left of each line.

options.description: Set numbering style for body lines (a=all, t=non-empty, n=none, p=regex)

options.use_case: Number every line including empty ones

options.description: Only number lines matching regular expression
options.use_case: Number only lines matching a pattern

options.description: Separator string between line number and text

options.use_case: Start numbering from a specific number

options.description: Number of blank lines to count as one
options.use_case: Treat multiple blank lines as one

misconceptions.title: Modifies original file
misconceptions.reality: nl only displays numbered output to stdout. It does not modify the original file.
misconceptions.tip: Use redirection to save numbered output: 'nl file.txt > numbered.txt'

misconceptions.title: Same as cat -n
misconceptions.reality: nl offers more formatting options (separators, increments, selective numbering) than 'cat -n'
misconceptions.tip: Use nl when you need advanced formatting options

common_pitfalls.description: By default, nl numbers all lines including empty ones
common_pitfalls.solution: Use '-bt' option to number only non-empty lines

common_pitfalls.description: Default tab separator might not be visible in some terminals
common_pitfalls.solution: Use '-s' option to specify a visible separator like ': ' or ' | '

related_commands.description: cat -n also numbers lines but with fewer formatting options
grep -n shows line numbers, nl adds numbers to all lines
sed can also add line numbers with '=' command

best_practices: Use '-bt' to skip empty lines when they're not needed
Use custom separator '-s' for better readability
Combine with other text processing commands via pipes
Redirect output to save numbered version: 'nl file.txt > numbered.txt'
